speaker: Doctor
text: I will begin by asking if you have experienced any pain in the affected eye or noticed a sudden increase in the number of spots, as this helps differentiate between retinal issues and intraocular inflammation. Additionally, have you noticed any floaters that seem to move with your eye movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and prior fungal esophagitis, I am concerned about opportunistic infections like CMV retinitis or Toxoplasmosis. I need to visualize the retina immediately to assess for characteristic lesions. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in an AIDS patient is highly characteristic of Cytomegalovirus retinitis. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other opportunistic infections, I need to check your current immune status. REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count

speaker: Doctor
text: The severely depressed CD4 count of 36/mm3 combined with the classic "pizza pie" appearance of hemorrhages and yellow-white opacities on fundoscopy confirms Cytomegalovirus retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis
